text:
jess: Heads-up: noticed a cluster of small spikes in provisional token usage tied to background-embed batches + mid-stream toolcall truncation. Looks like we charged parent session + child toolcall on reconnects.

omar: Can you paste one trace id?

jess: trace=trc_8492. Quick timeline: client starts stream -> background embed job fires async toolcall -> model-worker truncates toolcall (TTL) -> client reconnects and resumes main stream -> ledger shows provisional charges for both parent and toolcall child, and then both got confirmed later.

kevin: Hmm. Are we emitting any session anchors from the worker into the embedding subcall? If not, child toolcall may be treated as an independent session.

jess: Exactly. Embeds are spun up without parent-session header unless the worker explicitly forwards it. We also lost the final EOF checkpoint because truncation happened mid-toolcall.

lia: Proposal: checkpoint_v2 API that (1) requires sessions propagated into any internal toolcall, (2) includes token-range windows for child calls, and (3) supports an atomic ledger dry-run and reconcile endpoint for ops.

kevin: Dry-run is key. We should be able to POST a session reconciliation request and get back a delta without mutating ledger state (so ops can inspect before accepting).

jess: Example checkpoint_v2 payload (sketch):

```
POST /v2/checkpoint
Headers: X-RW-Session: rw-sess-900
Body: {
  "session": "rw-sess-900",
  "seq": 412,
  "confirmed_tokens": 128,
  "children": [
    {"id":"toolcall-77","parent_seq":410,"token_window": [100,128], "checksum":"sha256:abc"}
  ],
  "final": false
}
```

jess: Ledger semantics idea: provisional credits are applied as they occur. Checkpoints advance a confirmed pointer per session. When a child toolcall checkpoint arrives, the ledger subtracts any overlapping window from the parent's provisional balance if overlap_checksum matches. If checksum mismatch, mark for manual reconcile.

omar: For UX, add a "Reconcile (dry-run)" CTA in request detail that shows proposed token adjustments, audit reasons, and an accept button to apply. Also show provisional vs confirmed columns and a small timeline.

kevin: Telemetry to add: provisional_to_confirm_ratio (per-model, per-region), session_checkpoint_rate, checkpoint_ack_latency. Also a histogram for token_overlap_count for child calls. Alert if provisional_to_confirm_ratio > 0.1 for 2 consecutive minutes for a canary cohort.

lia: Ops safety: new endpoints gated by feature flag checkpoint_v2. Rollout: 1) router forwards X-RW-Session/X-RW-Seq into worker and internal toolcalls, 2) model-workers opt-in to emit v2 checkpoints, 3) ledger supports dry_reconcile API, 4) console surfaces reconciliation actions.

jess: Quick debug snippet for traces:

```
curl -H "X-RW-Session: rw-sess-900" -H "X-RW-Seq: 412" \
  https://router.internal.redwood/api/stream/trace/trc_8492
```

kevin: Audit trail: every dry_reconcile should produce a proposal id and not be allowed to mutate confirmed balances until accepted by an operator. We should attach a git-like diff of token adjustments to the audit record.

lia: Minor UX ask: console should highlight canary traffic in the request list and show a small badge if a session has unresolved child overlaps. That helps on-call spot canary regressions quickly.

deploy-bot: deploy: rolling router change (forward session headers into internal toolcalls) deployed to canary (5% traffic).

omar: Thanks. I'll open a short design doc: checkpoint_v2 proto, ledger dry_run API, console reconcile flow, alerting. Assigning to billing/infra for implementation planning.

jess: Filed: https://git.redwood/repo/issue/788 (draft). Meeting to sync Monday 9am PT.

kevin: One more: make sure background-embed library in runtime exposes a helper to propagate parent session headers by default. Saves a lot of footguns.

lia: Agreed. OK team, next steps: infra to implement header forwarding and ledger dry_run; billing to design finalization rules; console to mock reconcile UI. We'll coordinate on the doc. :white_check_mark:
